<query>I noticed the trainer at work only adjusts his broom when he’s near me, like he wants to impress me silently. Can someone’s body language really reveal feelings they won’t admit? Sometimes I feel like I’m the only one who catches these little signs of secret admiration.</query>
<response>Yes, body language often reveals emotions people don’t explicitly express. Subtle cues like adjusted posture, eye contact, or repetitive gestures (like the broom adjustment) can signal interest, nervousness, or even admiration, even if the person isn’t consciously trying to impress anyone. However, context matters—his behavior might also stem from habit, focus on his work, or social politeness. If you’re curious, observe broader patterns over time, but avoid overinterpreting. Sometimes, people act on instinct without realizing it. For now, trust your perception, but also consider that his actions might not be about you specifically. Focus on your own work, and let clarity emerge naturally.</response>
